elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: IBM may assign all or any part of the Agreement without MSL's consent to any IBM affiliate or subsidiary, although written notice is required.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: IBM may assign without MSL's consent to a successor by way of merger, upon written notice.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: IBM may assign without MSL's consent to a successor by way of acquisition, upon written notice.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: IBM may assign without MSL's consent to a successor through a sale of all or substantially all of the assets or business to which the Agreement relates, upon written notice.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The general restriction requires the other Party's prior written approval, and the MSL-specific provisions separately require IBM's prior written consent or approval for MSL assignments.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence states that required approval may not be unreasonably withheld or delayed, and the MSL Related Company provision repeats that standard.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No provision prohibits assignment to an IBM competitor. MSL could assign to a competitor if IBM approved.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right on Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The clause grants MSL no termination right arising from IBM's change of control.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor.
elements.evidence: IBM may assign without MSL's consent to successors arising through merger, acquisition, reorganization, or a sale of all or substantially all relevant assets or business.

elements.element: Customer must give written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: IBM's successor-assignment right is expressly conditioned on written notice to MSL.

elements.element: Vendor may assign without consent to a successor.
elements.evidence: MSL receives no successor carve-out. The notice and assumption provisions for an MSL sale or merger do not override the provisions requiring IBM's prior approval for MSL assignments.

elements.element: Vendor must give written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: MSL must immediately notify IBM when it decides to undertake specified sale, merger, or ownership-transfer transactions, but the clause does not require that notice to be written and does not tie it to a permitted successor assignment.

elements.element: Any Customer assignment other than to a successor requires Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: IBM may assign without MSL's consent to an IBM affiliate or subsidiary, which is an assignment other than to a successor unless that affiliate or subsidiary independently qualifies as one.

elements.element: Vendor consent required for Customer's other assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For IBM assignments that remain subject to approval, the opening sentence provides that approval may not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

elements.element: Any Vendor assignment other than to a successor requires Customer consent.
elements.evidence: All MSL assignments, including assignments to an MSL Related Company, remain subject to IBM's prior written consent or approval.

elements.element: Customer consent required for Vendor's other assignments may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence applies a reasonableness standard to required approval, and the MSL Related Company provision expressly states that IBM's consent may not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.

result.reason: The redline implements the principal IBM affiliate and successor carve-outs and imposes a reasonableness standard on consent, but it omits the absolute prohibition on assignment by MSL to an IBM competitor. It also fails the fallback because MSL has no consent-free successor-assignment right or written-notice obligation, while IBM affiliate assignments are exempted from consent. The edit is not minimal because it reaches neither complete position and extends the new reasonableness standard to subcontracting. The clause also retains duplicative MSL restrictions and the incomplete fragment 'MSL shall,' although the added IBM carve-out is otherwise structured to avoid conflict with the general prohibition.
